'''Peter Gavin Hall''' {{post-nominals|country=AUS|AO|FAA|FRS}}<ref name=rsbm>{{cite journal|last1=Robinson|first1=John|last2=Welsh|first2=Alan H.|title=Peter Gavin Hall. 20 November 1951 – 9 January 2016|journal=[[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]]|volume=64|pages=207–229|year=2018|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|issn=0080-4606|doi=10.1098/rsbm.2017.0035|doi-access=free}}</ref> (20 November 1951 – 9 January 2016) was an Australian researcher in [[probability theory]] and [[mathematical statistics]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hall, Peter Gavin — Person |url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P004649b.htm |access-date=2025-07-30 |website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Innovation |language=en-gb}}</ref> The [[American Statistical Association]] described him as one of the most influential and prolific theoretical statisticians in the history of the field.<ref name="amstat">{{cite web | url=http://www.amstat.org | title=American Statistical Association, Obituary – Peter G. Hall | access-date=12 January 2016}}</ref>
The School of Mathematics and Statistics Building at [[The University of Melbourne]] was renamed the Peter Hall building in his honour on 9 December 2016.<ref name="PeterHallBuidling">{{cite web|title=University of Melbourne Media Release: Peter Hall Building|url=http://newsroom.melbourne.edu/tags/peter-hall-building|date=10 October 2019}}</ref><ref>[http://www.ms.unimelb.edu.au/Personnel/profile.php?PC_id=308 University of Melbourne, School of Mathematics and Statistics: Professor Peter Hall] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071017154623/http://ms.unimelb.edu.au/Personnel/profile.php?PC_id=308 |date=17 October 2007 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://hallmemorialconference.ucdavis.edu|title=Peter Hall Memorial Conference|website=hallmemorialconference.ucdavis.edu}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://peterhallmemorial.ucdavis.edu|title=Peter Gavin Hall|website=peterhallmemorial.ucdavis.edu}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.stat-center.pku.edu.cn/Peter_Gavin_Hall|title=Peter_Gavin_Hall|last=Levey|website=www.stat-center.pku.edu.cn}}</ref>

==Education==
Hall attended [[Sydney Technical High School]] in Bexley, NSW during the years 1964–1969. He placed consistently high in examination results and in his final year, was among the top achievers in his form, and the winner of Old Boys' Union Mathematics prize.<ref>STHS Journal, 1970</ref>

Hall earned his [[Doctor of Philosophy]] degree at the [[University of Oxford]] in 1976 for research supervised by [[John Kingman]].<ref name=DPhil>{{cite thesis|degree=DPhil|publisher=University of Oxford|url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/OXVU1:LSCOP_OX:oxfaleph019868340|title=Some Problems in Limit Theory for Stochastic Processes and Sums of Random Variables|first=Peter Gavin|last=Hall|date=1976|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.457865}}|website=bodleian.ox.ac.uk|oclc=500461400}}{{Dead link|date=January 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref><ref name=mathgene>{{MathGenealogy|id=79323}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Hall was an author in probability and statistics.  [[MathSciNet]] lists 606 publications as of January 2016.  He made contributions to nonparametric statistics, in particular for curve estimation and resampling: the bootstrap method, smoothing, density estimation, and bandwidth selection.  He worked on numerous applications across fields of economics, engineering, physical science and biological science.  Hall also made contributions to surface roughness measurement using fractals.  In probability theory he made many contributions to limit theory, spatial processes and [[stochastic geometry]].  His paper "Theoretical comparison of bootstrap confidence intervals" (Annals of Statistics, 1988) has been reprinted in the ''Breakthroughs in Statistics'' collection.

He was an [[Australian Research Council]] (ARC) Laureate Fellow at the School of Mathematics and Statistics, [[University of Melbourne]],<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.arc.gov.au/media/fl11/pdf/Peter_Hall_bio.pdf |title=Professor Peter Hall|work=2011 Australian Laureate Fellows |access-date=2014-05-12 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140212013138/http://www.arc.gov.au/media/fl11/pdf/Peter_Hall_bio.pdf |archive-date=12 February 2014}}</ref> and also had a joint appointment at [[University of California Davis]].<ref name="ucdavis">{{cite web | title=UCDavis – History of the Department of Statistics | url=http://anson.ucdavis.edu/about/history | access-date=4 March 2011 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110629170808/http://anson.ucdavis.edu/about/history | archive-date=29 June 2011}}</ref> He previously held a professorship at the Centre for Mathematics and its Applications at the [[Australian National University]].

===Published books===

* P. Hall (1992): ''The Bootstrap and Edgeworth Expansion'', Springer, New York. {{isbn|0-387-97720-1}}

==Personal life==
Peter Hall was born to [[radiophysics]] and [[radio astronomy]] pioneer [[Ruby Payne-Scott]] and telephone technician William Holman Hall. His younger sister is artistic photographer and sculptor, [[Fiona Margaret Hall]].<ref>{{cite book|last1=Goss|first1=W. Miller|last2=McGee|first2=Richard X.|title=Under the Radar: The First Woman in Radio Astronomy|date=24 September 2009|publisher=Springer-Verlag|location=Berlin|isbn=978-3-642-03141-0}}</ref> Hall was a keen photographer with a special interest in train photography.<ref name=amstat /> He enjoyed travel and was a regular visitor to many universities around the
world. He died of leukaemia in Melbourne on 9 January 2016. He is survived by his wife, Jeannie.
